excerpt: Chopper: removing spam tokens from RAG context (mmBERT / Qwen width-slice choppers, Wikipedia chains dataset) - wiiiktor/chopper_demo
content_html:
70-second video: youtu.be/KMvmdXCEOJU

Chopper 0.3B close to Opus 5.5 in cutting out the best pieces

Chops are pieces cut out of the original text snippets retrieved from a database or a long conversation: exact quotes, never rewritten. The chopper (mmBERT, 0.31B) makes them; for comparison, Claude Opus 5.5 makes them too, also forced to quote directly.

What is new: a new method, invented in November 2026 in Poland (EU). The chopper is not an LLM summarising the snippets: a small encoder reads the question and all 20 snippets together in one pass and marks every word keep or drop. There is no text generation, so it is fast: 50 ms per question (20 snippets, ~2,400 tokens) on a consumer-grade GPU (RTX 3090), 36 ms with mmBERT-small.

One database retrieval per question, even at 4 hops. Every result below uses a single retrieval: each question gets its 20 snippets once, the chopper cuts them once, and Qwen3-14B answers once. There are no follow-up searches and no second rounds, so a 4-hop question has to be chained from one cut.

A reranker that also gives you the chops

One model replaces both the reranker and the compressor. Full comparison: below.

Qwen3-14B answering from full snippets or just short chops

400 MuSiQue questions, 100 each at 1, 2, 3 and 4 hops, each with its own 20 retrieved snippets. Qwen3-14B (4-bit, no fine-tuning, no thinking mode) answers from the given text only; gpt-5.6-luna judges. Length = prompt tokens. Each score counts every correct answer, including those from incomplete chops; the number in brackets counts only questions whose chops kept every hop and the answer.

Qwen3-14B: all snippets vs chops from the chopper vs chops from Opus 5.5

Read each diagram like website traffic: questions flow left to right, and at every hop the ones whose fact the chops missed drop out; the last stage is Qwen3-14B answering correctly. Top: all 20 retrieved snippets. Middle: the chopper's chops. Bottom: Opus 5.5's chops.

The last stage is the table's score; the lighter block under it counts answers Qwen got right from incomplete chops, and the number in brackets leaves them out. More: docs/DETAILS.md §7.

Also a reranker: ranking and chopping in one pass

The chopper scores every passage while it chops (mean p(KEEP) of the passage's 16 most likely tokens). On the 8-language rerank holdout (400 queries, 16 passages each, never trained on), ranked against dedicated rerankers:

ranking 16 passages nDCG@10 Hit@1 GPU time per query (RTX 3090)
chopper, mmBERT-base (0.31B), one pass 0.973 0.972 0.20 s, chops + ANSWER/SEARCH included
bge-reranker-v2-m3 (0.57B) 0.984 0.985 0.20 s
Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B 0.977 0.972 0.77 s
Qwen3-Reranker-4B 0.986 0.990 3.3 s

The chopper was never trained to rank, yet it is within about one point of the best rerankers at the speed of the fastest, so a pipeline can drop its reranker: retrieve → chopper gives the ranking and the quotes. Caveats (this test is easy for every model; the labels favour Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B) in the details.

Against other context compressors

Same 400 questions, same 20 snippets, same Qwen3-14B prompt; each compressor cuts the snippets once:

Qwen3-14B answering from tokens 1-hop 2-hop 3-hop 4-hop
all 20 snippets (no compression) 2,620 84 28 22 12
LLMLingua-2 (Microsoft), rate 0.1 374 28 6 2 4
Provence (Naver), its default threshold 0.1 263 77 27 26 16
Provence, threshold 0.5 152 71 24 21 11
chops from the chopper, mmBERT-small (0.14B) 217 72 49 32 23
chops from the chopper, mmBERT-base (0.31B) 228 83 48 45 29

LLMLingua-2 drops tokens without looking at the question, so the facts a chain needs rarely survive. Provence reads the question but prunes each snippet on its own. To be fair to them: the chopper was trained on MuSiQue's train split (this test uses its dev split) and on other multi-hop data, while both were trained for general single-passage use.

Chopper 🔪 keep only the part of RAG that answers the question

Standard RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) pastes whole passages into your model's context, and they stay there. About 95% of those tokens don't help. After a few lookups, a long session is mostly retrieval spam.

Chopper is a small model that reads the retrieved passages first and keeps only the fragments that matter. Your model then sees ~100 tokens instead of ~3,000 per lookup, and a session can carry dozens of lookups.

question ─► retrieve 16 passages ─► 🔪 rank + chop in one pass ─► model answers, or asks one follow-up search
  • 🎯 Clean context: only useful fragments enter the session; the raw passages never stay.
  • ⚡ Less compute: the main model reads 2–5% of the retrieved text.
  • 🏅 Also a reranker: the same pass ranks the passages almost as well as bge-reranker-v2-m3 (nDCG@10 0.973 vs 0.984, 8 languages), at the same speed. No separate reranker needed.
  • 🔗 Multi-hop works: the model writes a follow-up question when a fact is missing, and searches again.
  • 🏠 Built on one home GPU: every dataset and model here was made on a single RTX 3090 (some labels came from APIs).

Results at a glance
retrieved text the main model reads 2–5% (about 20–40× less); the answer is still in the kept text for 85% of HotpotQA and 69% of TriviaQA questions
"nothing here": pools whose answer was deleted (8 languages, business documents) asks to search again 67% of the time, keeps 1.4% of the text
ranking 16 passages (8-language holdout, 400 queries) nDCG@10 0.973, vs bge-reranker-v2-m3 0.984 and Qwen3-Reranker-4B 0.986; 0.20 s like bge, 16× faster than Qwen-4B, chops included (details)
chopping time per lookup (RTX 3090) 155 ms (separate mmBERT) · 277 ms (built into MiniCPM3-4B)
4-hop MuSiQue questions answered correctly by Qwen3-14B, one retrieval 12% → 29% with the chopper's chops instead of all 20 snippets (11× fewer tokens); with Opus 5.5's chops: 43%
Polish questions (PoQuAD, PolQA) answered correctly by Qwen3-14B 85.6% from the Polish chopper's chops (255 tokens) vs 85.2% from all 16 snippets (3,856 tokens)
license MIT: free for commercial use, weights and code. The closest alternatives, Provence and XProvence (Naver, sentence pruning + reranking), are CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: non-commercial only

In training (Nov 2026), suggested by the OPI PIB AI Lab: the same Polish chopper recipe on two Polish encoders, pl-ModernBERT-base from OPI PIB (results expected about 16 Nov) and polish-roberta-base-8k (8k context, about 18 Nov), compared with mmBERT-base-pl on the same 856 Polish questions. Restarted 15 Nov with the training data fitted to the Polish tokenizers (why).

Long-conversation memory results (LoCoMo, LongMemEval) are in the details: there the 4B answering model is the limit.

Pick your chopper

🟧 universal 🟪 integrated
what it is a separate small encoder (mmBERT-base, 0.31B, recommended; or mmBERT-small, 0.14B; both also in Polish versions) a 20% slice of MiniCPM3-4B's own weights + a small LoRA
works with any answering model: text in, text out MiniCPM3-4B
extra memory 0.31B / 0.14B weights 45M parameters; reads the model's own cache
weights 🤗 wiiiktor/chopper_mmbert 🤗 wiiiktor/chopper_minicpm3

Start with the universal one. The integrated one is the long-term bet: trained together with a model from the start, it should become almost free. If you pretrain models and want to build that, contact wiiiktor.

Quick start

In your own RAG pipeline (LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack or plain Python):

pip install chopper-rag                  # or "chopper-rag[langchain]", [llama-index], [haystack], [all]

As a tool for Claude (Claude Code, Claude Desktop or any MCP client): pip install "chopper-rag[mcp]", then claude mcp add chopper -- chopper-mcp. Claude can then call chop_passages / chop_files to read a few quotes instead of whole documents, or rank_passages to rerank; setup in integrations/chopper-rag.

from chopper_rag import Chopper
chopper = Chopper.from_pretrained(variant="base")          # or "small"; for Polish "base-pl", "small-pl"
result = chopper.run("When was the Eiffel Tower completed?", passages)   # passages: list of retrieved texts
print([c.text for c in result.chops], result.decision)    # exact quotes + ANSWER / SEARCH
print(result.ranking(top_k=5))                             # the same pass as a reranker: [(passage_index, relevance), ...]

Framework examples: integrations/chopper-rag. Listed in the LangChain integrations (ChopperCompressor). Or try the demo in this repo:

pip install -r requirements.txt

# your documents (a folder of .txt / .md, or a .jsonl with "title" and "text") + any Hugging Face causal LM
python operator-for-llm-with-mmbert.py --docs my_docs/ --model <hf model id> \
       --ask "Who founded the company that distributed the film UHF?"

# leave out --ask for an interactive session; it shows how many tokens plain RAG would have added

Weights download from Hugging Face on first use. Training data: 🤗 wiiiktor/chopper_demo.

Want the details?

Everything else is on one page, docs/DETAILS.md:

  • how it works: double prefill, rollback, the answer-or-search decision;
  • datasets and training on one GPU;
  • all results, including the search loop and the 8-language rerank pilot;
  • rewiring a model into its own chopper and what comes next;
  • credits, licenses and related work.

Credits

Built on mmBERT (JHU CLSP), MiniCPM3-4B (OpenBMB), Qwen3, Qwen3-Embedding and Qwen3-Reranker (Qwen team), bge-reranker (BAAI); labels and judgements also came from Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) and gpt-5.6-luna / GPT-6 Luna (OpenAI). Compared with LLMLingua-2 (Microsoft) and Provence (Naver). Data: the MuSiQue, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, TriviaQA, QASPER, Multi-Session Chat, WildChat, FineWeb, Wikipedia, LoCoMo and LongMemEval datasets; for Polish, PoQuAD and PolQA (IPI PAN). Our memory evaluation follows Memory Tax (He et al., 2026) and compares with MemT-1.0 (MemTensor, 2026). Full table with licenses: docs/DETAILS.md.

Licenses

Commercial use is allowed. The mmBERT choppers and all code are MIT. For comparison, Naver's Provence and XProvence context pruners are licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (no commercial use, no derivatives).

what license
mmBERT choppers, incl. Polish (mmbert-base, mmbert-small, mmbert-base-pl, mmbert-small-pl) MIT (as mmBERT)
code in this repo (LICENSE) and pip install chopper-rag MIT
MiniCPM3 chopper MiniCPM Model License (as MiniCPM3-4B)
training data wiiiktor/chopper_demo CC BY-SA 4.0 (share-alike from HotpotQA, Wikipedia and PolQA); Polish parts: PoQuAD CC BY 4.0, PolQA CC BY-SA 4.0

Some labels came from Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI Luna models, used to train a non-competing extraction tool; see docs/DETAILS.md.

Bored with reading LLMs' outputs? See also my other project, control_room: a VS Code panel for Claude Code that shows each answer as cards, charts and clickable options instead of a wall of text.

70-second video: youtu.be/KMvmdXCEOJU

Chopper 0.3B close to Opus 5.5 in cutting out the best pieces

Chops are pieces cut out of the original text snippets retrieved from a database or a long conversation: exact quotes, never rewritten. The chopper (mmBERT, 0.31B) makes them; for comparison, Claude Opus 5.5 makes them too, also forced to quote directly.

What is new: a new method, invented in November 2026 in Poland (EU). The chopper is not an LLM summarising the snippets: a small encoder reads the question and all 20 snippets together in one pass and marks every word keep or drop. There is no text generation, so it is fast: 50 ms per question (20 snippets, ~2,400 tokens) on a consumer-grade GPU (RTX 3090), 36 ms with mmBERT-small.
One database retrieval per question, even at 4 hops. Every result below uses a single retrieval: each question gets its 20 snippets once, the chopper cuts them once, and Qwen3-14B answers once. There are no follow-up searches and no second rounds, so a 4-hop question has to be chained from one cut.

A reranker that also gives you the chops

One model replaces both the reranker and the compressor. Full comparison: below.

Qwen3-14B answering from full snippets or just short chops

400 MuSiQue questions, 100 each at 1, 2, 3 and 4 hops, each with its own 20 retrieved snippets. Qwen3-14B (4-bit, no fine-tuning, no thinking mode) answers from the given text only; gpt-5.6-luna judges. Length = prompt tokens. Each score counts every correct answer, including those from incomplete chops; the number in brackets counts only questions whose chops kept every hop and the answer.

Qwen3-14B: all snippets vs chops from the chopper vs chops from Opus 5.5

Read each diagram like website traffic: questions flow left to right, and at every hop the ones whose fact the chops missed drop out; the last stage is Qwen3-14B answering correctly. Top: all 20 retrieved snippets. Middle: the chopper's chops. Bottom: Opus 5.5's chops.

The last stage is the table's score; the lighter block under it counts answers Qwen got right from incomplete chops, and the number in brackets leaves them out. More: docs/DETAILS.md §7.

Also a reranker: ranking and chopping in one pass

The chopper scores every passage while it chops (mean p(KEEP) of the passage's 16 most likely tokens). On the 8-language rerank holdout (400 queries, 16 passages each, never trained on), ranked against dedicated rerankers:

ranking 16 passages nDCG@10 Hit@1 GPU time per query (RTX 3090)
chopper, mmBERT-base (0.31B), one pass 0.973 0.972 0.20 s, chops + ANSWER/SEARCH included
bge-reranker-v2-m3 (0.57B) 0.984 0.985 0.20 s
Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B 0.977 0.972 0.77 s
Qwen3-Reranker-4B 0.986 0.990 3.3 s

The chopper was never trained to rank, yet it is within about one point of the best rerankers at the speed of the fastest, so a pipeline can drop its reranker: retrieve → chopper gives the ranking and the quotes. Caveats (this test is easy for every model; the labels favour Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B) in the details.

Against other context compressors

Same 400 questions, same 20 snippets, same Qwen3-14B prompt; each compressor cuts the snippets once:

Qwen3-14B answering from 代币 1-hop 2-hop 3-hop 4-hop
all 20 snippets (no compression) 2,620 84 28 22 12
LLMLingua-2 (Microsoft), rate 0.1 374 28 6 2 4
Provence (Naver), its default threshold 0.1 263 77 27 26 16
Provence, threshold 0.5 152 71 24 21 11
chops from the chopper, mmBERT-small (0.14B) 217 72 49 32 23
chops from the chopper, mmBERT-base (0.31B) 228 83 48 45 29

LLMLingua-2 drops tokens without looking at the question, so the facts a chain needs rarely survive. Provence reads the question but prunes each snippet on its own. To be fair to them: the chopper was trained on MuSiQue's train split (this test uses its dev split) and on other multi-hop data, while both were trained for general single-passage use.

Chopper 🔪 keep only the part of RAG that answers the question

Standard RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) pastes whole passages into your model's context, and they stay there. About 95% of those tokens don't help. After a few lookups, a long session is mostly retrieval spam.

Chopper is a small model that reads the retrieved passages first and keeps only the fragments that matter. Your model then sees ~100 tokens instead of ~3,000 per lookup, and a session can carry dozens of lookups.

question ─► retrieve 16 passages ─► 🔪 rank + chop in one pass ─► model answers, or asks one follow-up search
  • 🎯 Clean context: only useful fragments enter the session; the raw passages never stay.
  • ⚡ Less compute: the main model reads 2–5% of the retrieved text.
  • 🏅 Also a reranker: the same pass ranks the passages almost as well as bge-reranker-v2-m3 (nDCG@10 0.973 vs 0.984, 8 languages), at the same speed. No separate reranker needed.
  • 🔗 Multi-hop works: the model writes a follow-up question when a fact is missing, and searches again.
  • 🏠 Built on one home GPU: every dataset and model here was made on a single RTX 3090 (some labels came from APIs).

快速启动

In your own RAG pipeline (LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack or plain Python):

pip install chopper-rag                  # or "chopper-rag[langchain]", [llama-index], [haystack], [all]

As a tool for Claude (Claude Code, Claude Desktop or any MCP client): pip install "chopper-rag[mcp]", then claude mcp add chopper -- chopper-mcp. Claude can then call chop_passages / chop_files to read a few quotes instead of whole documents, or rank_passages to rerank; setup in integrations/chopper-rag.

from chopper_rag import Chopper
chopper = Chopper.from_pretrained(variant="base")          # or "small"; for Polish "base-pl", "small-pl"
result = chopper.run("When was the Eiffel Tower completed?", passages)   # passages: list of retrieved texts
print([c.text for c in result.chops], result.decision)    # exact quotes + ANSWER / SEARCH
print(result.ranking(top_k=5))                             # the same pass as a reranker: [(passage_index, relevance), ...]

Framework examples: integrations/chopper-rag. Listed in the LangChain integrations (ChopperCompressor). Or try the demo in this repo:

pip install -r requirements.txt

# your documents (a folder of .txt / .md, or a .jsonl with "title" and "text") + any Hugging Face causal LM
python operator-for-llm-with-mmbert.py --docs my_docs/ --model <hf model id> \
       --ask "Who founded the company that distributed the film UHF?"

# leave out --ask for an interactive session; it shows how many tokens plain RAG would have added
